topics.flagship-ru-ua: A Russian drone strike on Dnipro's train station killed at least 13 people while two trains waited at the platform, according to Zelenskiy (7 outlets). Separately, a localized ceasefire around Oleshky entered its third day, with humanitarian aid expected to enter and landmines being cleared. Other single-source items report Russian missile and drone strikes on Kyiv, Merz accusing North Korea of threatening Europe by sending troops to fight for Russia, and debate over EU shadow-fleet sanctions if the US pulls back.
topics.flagship-ir-il: Yemeni officials appealed for international protection for civilians in Taiz as Houthi forces tightened their siege (3 outlets). Vance has reportedly written to Iran's security chief Rezaei urging a swift return to peace talks, while Trump warned Gulf states to 'prepare' (2 outlets). Single-source items report Iran claiming three tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz, Hegseth firing Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia over alleged leaks about the Iran war, and analysts saying Israel's election deadlock could leave room for new strikes on Iran.
topics.T15: A fire at the Savannah River National Laboratory in South Carolina triggered a site-area emergency, disrupting road, rail and air traffic; restrictions were reportedly lifted after no contamination was detected. Cyclone Arnab reportedly made landfall on the Andhra Pradesh coast, prompting evacuations in Odisha. Flooding in Hurricane, Utah, has left residents uncertain about state and federal aid.
topics.T01: Jordan's air strikes in southern Syria killed at least seven people, including three children, according to a single report. Pakistan disputed Afghan Taliban claims about cross-border shelling at Angoor Adda in South Waziristan that killed a civilian. Greece's foreign minister warned Turkey over a reported maritime delimitation deal with Egypt.
topics.T02: Strikes on a Darfur market in Sudan reportedly killed more than 100 people, including women and children, according to a rights group. In Yemen, fighting has displaced more than 281,000 people since August, the UN said, and Houthis are accused of depriving Taizz civilians of food and medicine. Nearly 6 million people in Haiti face severe hunger, and Myanmar has 16.2 million people needing aid.
topics.T03: Local authorities in Taiz, Yemen, called for a UN-backed investigation into reports that Houthi forces fired shells and rockets suspected of containing banned chemical substances; this is a single-source, unverified claim. Separately, samples from a barrel marked 'U.S. Army' found in Quebec are being tested for a possible neurotoxin.
topics.T04: The Ebola outbreak in the DRC has passed 10,000 cases, making it the second largest ever and the fastest growing in the country's history; the Africa CDC chief reportedly warned no country is safe. Nigeria has a confirmed Ebola case and is paying contacts to quarantine. Brazil confirmed a third Newcastle disease outbreak in poultry, prompting trade restrictions, and lumpy skin disease was reportedly detected at a research center near Moscow.
topics.T05: Stories are mostly commentary and scattered, with no single coherent development. Items include claims about the planning of Hasina's 2024 ouster in Bangladesh, Sweden's government deadlock, Russia's pledge of support for Cuba, and opinion pieces on Myanmar and 'regime change' trends.
topics.T06: Fallout continues from riots in France following October 17 nationwide protests, with the government pushing a bill that would make protesters pay up to €10,000 for damages. In Italy, Meloni called a Milan court's release of a riot suspect 'shameful'. Coverage frames this as a wave of youth-driven demonstrations across Europe.
topics.T07: Analysts attribute North Korea's recent flurry of missile tests in part to its closer relationship with Russia, and warn Russian help could worsen it (2 outlets). No specific new test details are given.
topics.T08: A 22-year-old Perth man was charged with allegedly preparing a terrorist attack after arrest by WA's Joint Counter Terrorism Team (7 outlets). Uganda reportedly foiled a terrorist attack near Kampala, leaving two suspects dead. Nigerian troops reportedly repelled attacks in Benue and Zamfara, and a man was sentenced for a 2023 Islamic State-inspired knife attack on a Surrey bus.
topics.T10: Reporting highlights US losses in the Iran war, including at least 45 MQ-9 Reapers and a $300 million radar destroyed in Jordan. The UK promised higher defense spending by 2030 without detail, and India approved $22 billion in military spending. China and Russia are reportedly developing anti-satellite weapons, and a DIA report shows China's Shenlong spaceplane with a second docked spacecraft.
topics.T11: India's INS Sahyadri sailed for the sea phase of a bilateral exercise with South Korea at Busan. The Malabar 2026 exercise involving the US, India, Japan and Australia is set for Nov. 5-12 south of Honshu. US Southern Command and Colombia will begin the Southern Vanguard exercise with 800 troops on November 2.
topics.T12: A cyberattack on the FEC delayed disclosure of big-donor political spending before the system was restored (5 outlets). Distributed Denial of Secrets reportedly released data on more than 40,000 DHS employees, and the Pentagon is treating freezer malfunctions at at least six military commissaries as a suspected cyberattack. Other items include a Sony ISP breach exposing 2.5 million records, an AfD breach, and record Q3 ransomware incidents.
topics.T13: More than 50,000 people have reportedly fled Ethiopia into Kenya after Moyale border clashes, according to UNHCR. The World Uyghur Congress warned of imminent deportation of two Uyghur men from Thailand to China. Other items are minor, including Nigerian returnees from Libya and vehicle arson in Ceuta.
topics.T14: Mike Waltz said a Cuban diplomat will be expelled from the US after an alleged attempt to assault an American diplomat during a confrontation at the UN (3 outlets).
topics.T16: Israel's election is deadlocked, with Netanyahu's bloc holding a slight edge but no majority for either side; opposition candidate Eisenkot warned Netanyahu is trying to delegitimise the results. Flávio Bolsonaro reportedly escaped Brazil to the US with assistance that reportedly included Trump's help. In the US, the DOJ issued new subpoenas in an Alaska ballot spoiler-candidate probe ahead of the Nov. 3 midterms.

bluf: A Russian drone strike on Dnipro's train station killed at least 13 people while two trains waited at the platform, according to Zelenskiy, in a story carried by seven outlets. In Yemen, officials appealed for international help as Houthi forces tightened their siege of Taiz, and local authorities there reportedly seek a UN probe into suspected Houthi chemical weapon use, which is unverified and single-source. A cyberattack on the FEC delayed disclosure of big-donor political spending before the system was restored, with OpenSecrets saying 'disclosure delayed is disclosure denied.' Vance has reportedly written to Iran's security chief Rezaei urging a swift return to peace talks, while Trump warned Gulf states to 'prepare.' A 22-year-old Perth man was charged with allegedly planning a terrorist attack after arrest by WA's Joint Counter Terrorism Team. Separately, the DRC Ebola outbreak has passed 10,000 cases, becoming the second largest on record and the fastest growing in the country's history. Israel's election remains deadlocked with no clear majority for Netanyahu's bloc or its rivals.
